title: Plan tracker
summary: Where plan steps live: in the plan files, or in the project's GitHub Issues, and whether go-getter may create, comment on and close issues from a plan.

options.label: In the plan files
options.tradeoff: Steps and their state are Markdown in docs/plans, read offline and changed through git; teammates who do not use git do not see them, and nothing links a step to an issue.

options.label: In GitHub Issues, with the plan files holding the step text
options.tradeoff: A step that names an issue takes its state from the issue, so the work is visible where the team already tracks it; plan status needs gh and the network (the last state read is shown, marked stale, when it fails), and a step without an issue stays file-driven.

questions.prompt: May go-getter write to the tracker (create an issue from a step, comment, close)?

options.label: Yes, with a human approving each write
options.tradeoff: plan issue create, comment and close prompt before they run (a hand-over on hosts without native prompts); dry runs and reads never prompt.

options.label: No: go-getter only reads
options.tradeoff: A person creates and closes issues; plan status still shows their state.

options.label: Yes, without asking
options.tradeoff: Fastest, and the only writes are the three plan issue verbs, which refuse text containing a secret or personal data; an agent can still create, comment on and close issues unprompted, which others see.

questions.prompt: Which commands write to the tracker and so need a human? One prefix per spelling of the three verbs; add the way your project runs go-getter (for example .go-getter/bin/go-getter plan issue create).

decisions.title: Plan steps live in the plan files
decisions.body:
## Decision

Plan steps and their state live in the plan files under docs/plans; no tracker is read or written (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

The project keeps its plans in git and has no need to link steps to an issue tracker.

decisions.title: Plan steps live in GitHub Issues
decisions.body:
## Decision

A plan step that names a GitHub issue (an `Issue:` field) takes its state from the issue: closed as completed is done, closed as not planned is moved, an open issue is not done. A step without an issue stays file-driven, and the plan file is never rewritten to match (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

Work is visible where the team already tracks it, and issue text is read as data and never run as a command.

decisions.title: go-getter may write to the tracker with a human approving each write
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter plan issue create`, `comment` and `close` write to the tracker only after a human approves the command (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); a dry run and every read need no approval.

## Why

Writing is outward-facing and visible to others; the text sent is checked for secrets and personal data first.

guardrails.title: Writes to the plan tracker follow the project's answer

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given plan writes are visible to others, the project asked for a human on each, which the host must enforce since an instruction alone fails silently.

enforcement.check: Host ask rules and the pre-tool hook gate the commands that write to the tracker
Ask the user before running go-getter plan issue create, comment or close

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

The commands that write to the tracker (`plan issue create`, `comment`, `close`) need a human: do not run them yourself, ask the user to approve or run them. Hosts with project ask rules prompt natively; the others get a hand-over from the pre-tool hook. Raw `gh issue` and `gh api` commands are covered by the human-approval guardrail of the hitl pack, not by this one.

decisions.title: go-getter does not write to the tracker
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter plan issue` refuses to create, comment on or close issues; go-getter only reads issue state (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

People create and close the project's issues themselves.

guardrails.title: Writes to the plan tracker follow the project's answer

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the project chose that go-getter only reads the tracker, the CLI refuses writes and the instruction says why.

enforcement.check: Do not run go-getter plan issue create, comment or close; ask the user

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Do not write to the tracker from a plan: `go-getter plan issue create`, `comment` and `close` refuse while this answer is off. Ask the user to create or close an issue.

decisions.title: go-getter may write to the tracker without asking
decisions.body:
## Decision

`go-getter plan issue create`, `comment` and `close` run without a human approving each one (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}); the text they send is checked for secrets and personal data first, and raw `gh issue` commands stay gated by the hitl pack.

## Why

The project accepted the visibility of agent-written issues for less friction.

guardrails.title: Writes to the plan tracker follow the project's answer

frontmatter.derivation-note: Given the project chose no prompt for plan writes, the rule rests on the agent keeping to the verbs and the step text.

enforcement.check: Write to the tracker only through go-getter plan issue and only what the step says

guardrails.body:
## Guardrail

Write to the tracker only through `go-getter plan issue create`, `comment` and `close`, never with raw `gh issue` commands, and only what the plan step says. Advisory (tier 1): nothing prompts for these verbs.

decisions.title: The commands that write to the tracker are listed
decisions.body:
## Decision

The commands [{{answer.write-commands}}] need a human before they run (pack {{pack.id}}@{{pack.version}}).

## Why

A prompt matches the text of a command, so each way of running go-getter that the project uses is listed.
